newsitem.title: USA: Intel sees higher third quarter revenues.
newsitem.headline: Intel sees higher third quarter revenues.

text.p: Microprocessor giant Intel Corp. said Monday that strong sales were likely to push its revenues for the quarter higher than it previously expected.

Brightening the outlook for the entire personal computer industry, Intel said its revenues now appeared likely to be about 5 percent higher than its second-quarter revenues of $4.62 billion, rather than flat with that quarter as it once expected.

Intel provides the microprocessors for about 80 percent of the personal computers sold in the world. Because of that huge market share, analysts view its business as a mirror on the health of the PC industry generally.
When it reported its second-quarter earnings in July, it had forecast that third revenues would be flat with the earlier quarter.

Intel also said Monday that its gross margin -- a key indicator of profitability -- will also be better in the third quarter than it previously thought. It said it will be above its target of 50 percent plus or minus a couple of points.

Intel said business levels were hard to predict because the semiconductor industry is currently in a so-called "turns" environment where manufacturers order chips just before they need them in the assembly line.
"Business levels are inherently difficult to predict and appear to be better than originally expected," the Santa Clara-based company said in a statement.
